This is an odd choice for a license. It's in our allow list, but that might be due to the fact that we generated code using Bison in the past. If we merge this as-is this would be the only code in our repository with this license. Is there any other license from our allowed list that you can use?

Hello @geraldcombs ,

From the options listed [here](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html_chunked/ChSrcContribute.html) as compatible licenses when `GPL version 2 or later` is not possible to use, the `GPL version 3 or later with the Bison parser exception` is what works best for us, so we would rather keep it.
Was any of this generated using Bison?

No. However, GPLv3 is a requirement and the above linked page states:

>Notable incompatible licenses include Apache 2.0, GPL 3.0, and LGPL 3.0.

While it also lists `GPL version 3 or later with the Bison parser exception` as an allowed license. Therefore, we decided to adhere to the Bison parser exception and use GPLv3.

We need to make the documentation more clear and remove that option. As @geraldcombs alluded to GPLv3 with Bison exception but without Bison code is just GPLv3, and unfortunately that is not currently an allowed license.
Marking as a draft until the licensing issue is sorted out.

> We need to make the documentation more clear and remove that option.

Proposed in !12533.

I understand that this issue was fixed - https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/19439#note_1625897602 , commit https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/commit/0ea6bbb9e3b2fe86842eee73125eb96c10d43412
In all cases, these are strings. Why are you using `memcmp`? When the "GDP" string is passed in as `data`, you test against all three and there is an illegal memory access.
This can happen more with various compiler optimizations that compare word at a time, etc.

As `epan/column-utils.h` says about `col_set_str`:
> the text won't be formatted or copied... Use this for simple static strings like protocol names Usually used to set const strings!

`protocol_str` is not const here, so it's declared on the stack. You have to use `col_add_str` instead.

It might be cleaner to, instead of `call_dissector_with_data` with various static const char*, to use a dissector table for `rf4ce_profile` with either string values (or the PROFILE_ID_ values) and call that. (I don't see what you're using that existing `FT_NONE` table for at all.)

This heuristic seems extremely weak and might trigger a log of false positives. Can we tighten it, or at least have it disable by default?

If we canot tighten it then we will likely have to disable it by default as it will generta way too many false positive.
